messages:
matt: Heads up — a couple of customers saw duplicate upstream requests (and billing spikes) when using the TS SDK on Node 20 with the global fetch. Repro steps below, can we triage?

tara: Uh oh. Which SDK version and do you have logs / request IDs?

matt: SDK v2.3.4. Logs show repeated POSTs with same payload after a transient 5xx, even though we configured retries=2. Request id: req_02X7Z2A. Snippet:```ts
// app.ts
import Redwood from '@redwood/inference';
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY, retries: 2 });
const ac = new AbortController();
const payload = { prompt: 'summarize', text: '...' };
await client.request('/generate', { method: 'POST', body: JSON.stringify(payload), signal: ac.signal });
```
Note: customers use Node 20.4 with experimental global fetch enabled, and some also have undici installed for older code paths.

julia: That combo rings a bell — streaming/body replay semantics differ between Node's global fetch and undici. If the SDK's retry logic attempts to re-send the same ReadableStream body it will fail to replay unless the body is clonable. In practice some setups silently fall back and end up duplicating attempts.

ryan: Can you repro locally? If we can get a minimal repro that would help. Also, do they set an idempotency key?

matt: Repro steps I used:
1) node 20.4
2) npm i @redwood/inference@2.3.4 undici@5.15.2
3) run this server that proxies to our hosted API and intentionally returns 502 once then 200.
I can attach the tiny repro gist. TL;DR: SDK retry path does a plain fetch() retry with the same body string, but when using a stream-backed body it ends up making two full POSTs to upstream.

julia: Ok — likely root cause: our retry code assumes body is a simple string/Buffer and does not defensively clone or re-serialize when fetch is stream-backed. With Node 20's fetch behavior the first attempt drains the stream, so a naive retry will either send an empty body or cause upstream to get a fully re-posted body depending on adapter behaviour. Mix-and-match of global fetch vs undici can cause both outcomes.

tara: Customer impact notes? Which customers and how widespread?

matt: Two mid-market customers reported extra invoices (small but visible). Both had long-running upload-like payloads (large prompt/attachments).

support-bot: Created ticket INC-9876, assigned to eng-runtime. Priority: high.

ryan: Short-term mitigations we can advise customers: 1) Add an Idempotency-Key header (server will dedupe). 2) Use a JSON string body (serialize with JSON.stringify) or wrap payload in a Blob/Buffer so it's cloneable. 3) Pin Node or undici versions where we have tested behavior (we have verified stable behaviour on Node 18 + undici shim).

julia: Long-term fix options: a) SDK should normalize request bodies and create a replayable representation for retries (clone as Buffer/Blob for non-streams). b) Detect Node global fetch + stream body and either error with clear guidance or auto-buffer small bodies (with size limit and warning). I'll draft a PR to add defensive buffering + idempotency guidance.

matt: I've notified the affected customers with the idempotency workaround. They confirmed temporary fix.

ryan: Assigning to eng-runtime (julia) to implement buffering + a telemetry flag so we can count occurrences. Also add a docs note about Node 20 fetch differences.

julia: Will send a short patch and release v2.4.0-rc1 that auto-buffers when body is JSON and under 1MB, and logs an explicit warning for larger bodies.

support-bot: Updated INC-9876 with status: in_progress, owner: julia.

matt: Thanks — will monitor for any more reports. :thumbsup:
